title: lean-misc-math: miscellaneous mathematical results formalised in Lean 4
description:
A Lean 4 library of miscellaneous classical and other mathematical results built on Mathlib.

This repository is the product of two different kinds of work, and the distinction is deliberate. The choice of which results to formalise, how they should be stated and in what generality, and which are worth publishing is the author's contribution, as is a best-effort read of each Lean statement against its informal claim. The Lean statements and their proofs are generated by Claude; the proofs are read by nobody. Both are checked by Lean's kernel and audited so that every declaration depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

The consequence worth internalising is that a mistake here will not be a wrong proof, because the kernel does not admit those. It will be a statement that does not say what it appears to say. A best-effort read is not a review: one person, no second reader, and no reading of the proof. Every result therefore ships an informal statement, a source, a provenance record and sanity checks, including a satisfiability witness for every hypothesis, so that a reader can check the correspondence in about thirty seconds without reading a proof. Users should verify that a statement says what they need before relying on it.

The selection and curation of results is the contribution being credited by a citation.
